description: A Geiger counter: random clicks at a rate set by a radiation level, played through a modelled speaker

params.text: Sets the radiation level, from 0.02 to 50 milliroentgen an hour, which is what sets how often a click happens

inputs.text: A rising edge fires one click, on top of whatever the radiation level is already producing
Adds to the radiation knob, 10V covering the knob's whole travel, with the total clamped to its ends

notes: the click rate is 21.666 clicks a second for each milliroentgen an hour, drawn one sample at a time from a random number, so the clicks are irregular rather than evenly spaced.
each click is a five-sample pulse through a 1250Hz lowpass and a 150Hz highpass and then a soft clipper, which is what gives it the knock of a small speaker rather than a bare tick.
the lamp lights on each click and fades over about a fifteenth of a second.
the knob draws a gold arc from its own position round to where the CV input has moved it, and the arc turns orange when the CV pushes the level past either end.

inputs.1:
0 to 10V · continuous · polyphonic

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
